arxiv-1902-08791.title: Local loop lemma
arxiv-1902-08791.creator: Miroslav Olšák
arxiv-1902-08791.description: Abstract We prove that an idempotent operation generates a loop from a strongly connected digraph containing directed cycles of all lengths under very mild (local) algebraic assumptions. Using the result, we reprove the existence of a weakest non-trivial idempotent equations, and that a strongly connected digraph with algebraic length 1 compatible with a Taylor term has a loop.

arxiv-2012-05548.title: Calculation of multipole moments of axistationary electrovacuum spacetimes
arxiv-2012-05548.creator: Gyula Fodor, Etevaldo dos Santos Costa Filho, Betti Hartmann
arxiv-2012-05548.description: Abstract The multipole moments of stationary axially symmetric vacuum or electrovacuum spacetimes can be expressed in terms of the power series expansion coefficients of the Ernst potential on the axis. In this paper we present a simpler, more efficient calculation of the multipole moments, applying methods introduced by Bäckdahl and Herberthson.

arxiv-2212-11529.title: A hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin method with characteristic variables for Helmholtz problems Published in Journal of Computational Physics (doi: 10.1016/j.jcp.2023.112459 ). Distributed under Creative Commons CC-BY 4.0 license.
arxiv-2212-11529.creator: Axel Modave, Théophile Chaumont-Frelet
arxiv-2212-11529.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Axel Modave, Théophile Chaumont-Frelet. A new hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin method, named the CHDG method, is proposed for solving time-harmonic scalar wave propagation problems. This method relies on a standard discontinuous Galerkin scheme with upwind numerical fluxes and high-order polynomial bases. Auxiliary unknowns corresponding to characteristic variables are defined at the interface between the elements, and the physical fields are eliminated to obtain a reduced system. The reduced system can be written as a fixed-point problem that can be solved with stationary iterative schemes.

arxiv-2309-13782.title: On the Computational Benefit of Multimodal Learning
arxiv-2309-13782.creator: Zhou Lu
arxiv-2309-13782.description: Abstract Human perception inherently operates in a multimodal manner. Similarly, as machines interpret the empirical world, their learning processes ought to be multimodal. The recent, remarkable successes in empirical multimodal learning underscore the significance of understanding this paradigm. Yet, a solid theoretical foundation for multimodal learning has eluded the field for some time.

arxiv-2405-16337.creator: Nathaniel WeirJohns Hopkins University nweir@jhu.edu, Muhammad KhalifaUniversity of Michigan khalifam@umich.edu, Linlu QiuMIT linluqiu@mit.edu, Orion WellerJohns Hopkins University oweller@cs.jhu.edu Peter ClarkAllen Institute for AI peterc@allenai.org
arxiv-2405-16337.description: Abstract Program synthesis with language models (LMs) has unlocked a large set of reasoning abilities; code-tuned LMs have proven adept at generating programs that solve a wide variety of algorithmic symbolic manipulation tasks (e.g. word concatenation). However, not all reasoning tasks are easily expressible as code, e.g. tasks involving commonsense reasoning, moral decision-making, and sarcasm understanding.

arxiv-2501-15535.creator: Benjamin Florentin
arxiv-2501-15535.description: Abstract . The Steklov spectrum of a smooth compact Riemannian manifold ( M , g ) (M,g) with boundary is the set of eigenvalues counted with multiplicities of its Dirichlet-to-Neumann map (DN map). Macrophage polarization along the M1/M2 axis exerts a decisive influence on tendon healing trajectories.
